experiences.description: Part of the Mercury Rewrite team at American Airlines, migrating a legacy Java RMI, in-memory architecture to Java microservices backed by a Couchbase data layer. Joined the project in March 2026 after a 3-month Java and Angular training program.
highlights: Loaded 250K fares (30+ sortable, filterable columns) from a 42-million-record Couchbase dataset directly into the UI, replacing an expensive row-by-partition query (about 8 minutes) with key-value lookups and in-memory deduplication in Java: roughly 45-60 seconds, about 8x faster.

Built an agentic mesh with custom AI agents that business analysts and developers use to generate user stories and estimate effort, cutting roughly 2 days of analyst work to about 1 hour and 1 day of developer estimation to about 30 minutes (approximate figures).
Owned the Marketlist feature end to end and led the design of its draft-table approach.
Created ops-core, a reusable framework now used by 3 modules, with more planned.
Received written recognition from the Project Manager for the quality of delivery as a fresher.

experiences.description: Built a quantum-resistant VPN as part of the internship.
highlights: Integrated Kyber (KEM) and Dilithium (signatures) into StrongSwan using liboqs.
Modified IKEv2 negotiation and the crypto backend for post-quantum key exchange and authentication; configured and tested tunnels with swanctl.
